messages: You pick up the ruler and run your sensitive fingers over it. The 4-7/8 inch mark shows signs of recent use - a deliberate measurement.
You carefully examine the broken lamp glass. The edges are too clean - this was deliberately broken to a specific size of exactly 4-7/8 inches.
Parkinson skillfully navigates the motor car through London streets to your destination.
The telegram reads: Mr. Carrados - Desperate situation - Accused of causing Knights Cross accident - I am innocent - Please help - Hutchins Signalman
You scan the newspapers with your fingertips. The financial pages show significant railway stock movements before the accident. Someone profited from this disaster.

Hutchins speaks nervously: Mr. Carrados I swear I checked that signal lamp before my shift. It showed clear when I looked. But they say it was broken - showing false clear when it should have shown danger.

The elderly Mead speaks reluctantly: I may have mentioned to Mr. Pendleton about the lamp glass sizes. He seemed very interested. Asked me specific measurements. But I never thought it would lead to this.
Pendleton speaks smoothly: Detective work Mr. Carrados? I am a stockbroker not a railway saboteur. I was at my club when the accident occurred. Ask anyone.
You do not have enough evidence yet to make an accusation. You need to examine all the key pieces of evidence first.
You examine the stock certificate carefully. It shows Pendleton purchased railway competitor stocks the day before the accident. The profit from the railway stock drop would have been substantial.

Pendletons voice falters. Very well. Yes I broke the lamp glass to exactly 4-7/8 inches - the width that would show a false clear signal. I knew from Mead that size would cause the accident. The stock profits were worth millions. Harold Pendleton is arrested. Justice is served.
Congratulations! You have solved the Knights Cross Signal Problem. Max Carrados remarkable deductive abilities and attention to precise details have brought a criminal to justice.
There is nothing of interest to examine here.
Harold Pendleton is not here. You should find him at his office in the City.
